ns2:section.sectionText: Food is an important medium of global processes and flows. This course will provide students with theories, concepts,and methods to enable them to critical understand contemporary issues of global hunger, food security, and transnational food politics. Utilizing materials from history, anthropology, sociology, geography, political science, and other social science disciplines, the course will enable students to pursue more advanced research interests about the global dimensions of food, production, distribution, and consumption.
